versions.title: 책이 여기 있어
versions.setting: 나비의 책 하나 · 벤치 근처 풀밭 길
versions.caregiverNote: 실수를 말하는 아이를 겁주지 않아요. 예문은 연습이고 실제 고백은 선택 뒤에 나와요.

scenes.title: 찾고 있는 책
scenes.narration: 앨리스가 나비의 책을 말없이 가져왔어요. 나비는 책을 찾아요.
scenes.action: 앨리스는 책을 들고 있어요. 나비가 주변을 둘러봐요. 각 화자의 앞모습을 보여 줘요. 할머니의 예문은 연습 설명이지 사건 고백이 아니에요.

lines.speaker: 나비
lines.text: 내 책 어디 있지?

lines.speaker: 부엉이 할머니
lines.text: 한 일을 말할 땐 “내가 그랬어”라고 할 수 있어.

scenes.title: 사실을 말하는 표현
scenes.narration: 앨리스가 나비에게 말할 때 쓸 표현을 우리에게 알려 줘요.
scenes.action: 앨리스는 아이를 향해 표현을 설명해요. 나비에게 실제로 고백하거나 책을 건네는 동작은 아직 없어요.

lines.speaker: 앨리스
lines.text: “내가 그랬어”는 영어로 “It was me”야.

scenes.title: 말을 꺼낼까?
scenes.narration: 나비는 아직 책이 어디 있는지 몰라요.
scenes.action: 선택한 갈래에서만 실제 고백해요. 두 갈래가 끝날 때까지 책은 앨리스가 계속 들고 있어요.

choices.label: 지금 사실을 말해요
choices.action: 앨리스가 나비에게 걸어가 멈춘 뒤 앞모습으로 대사해요. 책을 아직 돌려주지 않아요.

lines.speaker: 앨리스
lines.text: 내가 그랬어. 책을 가져왔어.

lines.speaker: 나비
lines.text: 돌려줄래?

lines.speaker: 앨리스
lines.text: 응. 미안해.

choices.label: 아직 말하지 않아요
choices.action: 앨리스는 책을 들고 말없이 잠깐 기다려요. 나비의 표정을 앞에서 보여 줘요. 할머니가 곁에 서고, 앨리스가 얼굴을 보여 주며 고백해요. 책은 아직 앨리스에게 있어요.

lines.speaker: 나비
lines.text: 책이 없어. 슬퍼.

lines.speaker: 앨리스
lines.text: 말하기가 떨려요.

lines.speaker: 부엉이 할머니
lines.text: 여기 있을게. 천천히 말해도 돼.

lines.speaker: 앨리스
lines.text: 내가 그랬어. 책을 가져왔어.

lines.speaker: 나비
lines.text: 이제 알겠어. 돌려줘.

scenes.title: 책을 돌려줄 때
scenes.narration: 이제 나비가 책을 받을 준비를 해요.
scenes.action: 둘이 서서 손이 닿는 거리를 확보해요. 앨리스의 “여기 있어”에 맞춰 나비에게 책을 한 번만 건네요. 나비의 답은 받은 뒤 해요. 두 친구가 앉아 말할 때도 얼굴을 보여 줘요. 마지막 초대에서는 앨리스가 정면으로 아이에게 말해요.

lines.speaker: 앨리스
lines.text: 여기 있어.

lines.speaker: 나비
lines.text: 책이 와서 좋아. 고마워.

lines.speaker: 앨리스
lines.text: 네가 좋으니 나도 좋아.

lines.speaker: 앨리스
lines.text: 같이 “내가 그랬어” 해 볼까? 듣기만 해도 돼.

recall.prompt: 모모의 공을 네가 옮겼어. 누가 옮겼냐고 물으면 어떻게 말할까? 조용히 들어도 돼.

versions.title: Here is the book
versions.goal: Use a short phrase to say what you did
versions.setting: One book belonging to Nabi · path near the bench
versions.caregiverNote: Do not frighten a child who tells about a mistake. The example is practice; the actual confession follows the choice.

scenes.title: The missing book
scenes.narration: Alice took Nabi’s book without telling him. Nabi is looking for it.
scenes.action: Alice holds the book. Nabi looks around. Keep each speaking face visible. Grandma’s example is a language model, not a confession about this event.

lines.speaker: Nabi
lines.text: Where is my book?

lines.speaker: Grandma Owl
lines.text: To say what you did, you can say “It was me.”

scenes.title: Words for telling what happened
scenes.narration: Alice shares words she can use before speaking to Nabi.
scenes.action: Alice explains the expression to the viewer. There is no actual confession to Nabi or book handoff yet.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “내가 그랬어” means “It was me” in English.

scenes.title: Will Alice speak?
scenes.narration: Nabi still does not know where the book is.
scenes.action: The actual confession happens only inside the chosen path. Alice keeps holding the book through the end of either path.

choices.label: Tell what happened now
choices.narration: Alice stops in front of Nabi.
choices.action: Alice walks to Nabi, stops, and speaks with her face visible. Do not return the book yet.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: It was me. I took the book.

lines.speaker: Nabi
lines.text: Can I have it back?

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: Yes. I’m sorry.

choices.label: Stay quiet for now
choices.action: Alice holds the book during a short silent pause. Show Nabi’s face. Grandma stands nearby, then Alice confesses with her face visible. The book remains with Alice.

lines.speaker: Nabi
lines.text: My book is gone. I’m sad.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: I feel wobbly about telling.

lines.speaker: Grandma Owl
lines.text: I’m here. You can take your time.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: It was me. I took the book.

lines.speaker: Nabi
lines.text: Now I know. Please give it back.

scenes.title: Time to return it
scenes.narration: Nabi is ready to receive the book.
scenes.action: Both stand within reach. Give the book once on Alice’s “Here it is.” Nabi answers after receiving it. If the friends sit, keep their speaking faces visible. For the final invitation, show Alice facing the child.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: Here it is.

lines.speaker: Nabi
lines.text: I’m happy my book is back. Thank you.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: You feel happy. I do too.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: Try “It was me” with me? You can just listen.

recall.prompt: You moved Momo’s ball. Someone asks who moved it. What could you say? Listening is okay.

lines.text: I left it right here. Where did it go?

lines.speaker: Grandma Owl
lines.text: To tell about a mistake, you can say “It was me,” then explain what happened.

scenes.title: Words for telling what happened
scenes.narration: Alice shares words she can use before speaking to Nabi.
scenes.action: Alice explains the expression to the viewer. There is no actual confession to Nabi or book handoff yet.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “내가 그랬어” means “It was me” in English. It tells what I did instead of hiding it.

scenes.title: Will Alice speak?
scenes.narration: Nabi still does not know where the book is.
scenes.action: The actual confession happens only inside the chosen path. Alice keeps holding the book through the end of either path.

choices.label: Explain and offer to return it
choices.narration: Alice stops in front of Nabi.
choices.action: Alice walks to Nabi, stops, and speaks with her face visible. Do not return the book yet.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: It was me. I wanted to see the pictures, so I took it without asking. I’m sorry.

lines.speaker: Nabi
lines.text: You had it while I was searching. I’d like it back.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: Yes. I’ll return it now.

choices.label: Stay silent a little longer
choices.action: Alice holds the book during a short silent pause. Show Nabi’s face. Grandma stands nearby, then Alice confesses with her face visible. The book remains with Alice.

lines.speaker: Nabi
lines.text: I feel frustrated because I keep looking and cannot find it.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: If I don’t say, Nabi will keep searching. Grandma, please stay beside me.

lines.speaker: Grandma Owl
lines.text: Yes. Take your time and use your own words.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: Nabi, it was me. I took it to see the pictures. I’m sorry I didn’t ask.

lines.speaker: Nabi
lines.text: Now I know where it is. Could you give it back?

scenes.title: Time to return it
scenes.narration: Nabi is ready to receive the book.
scenes.action: Both stand within reach. Give the book once on Alice’s “Here it is.” Nabi answers after receiving it. If the friends sit, keep their speaking faces visible. For the final invitation, show Alice facing the child.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: Here it is. Next time I’ll ask if I can look.

lines.speaker: Nabi
lines.text: Finding my book helps me feel calm. Thank you for telling me.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: I’m glad you feel better. You can look at it first now.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: Want to try “It was me”? You do not have to tell your own story. Listening is fine.

recall.prompt: Momo is searching for a ball. You remember moving it beside the house. How could you explain what happened and where it is? Quiet thinking is okay.
recall.example: It was me. I moved it beside the house. Let’s go and find it.

versions.title: 내가 아는 것, 나비가 아는 것
versions.goal: 말하기 어려운 마음과 친구가 모르는 상황을 함께 생각하며 사실과 수정을 전하기
versions.setting: 나비의 책 하나 · 벤치 근처 풀밭 길
versions.caregiverNote: 고백 뒤에도 친구에게 남은 감정을 인정해요. 아이에게 실제 잘못을 찾아 말하라고 요구하지 않아요.

scenes.title: 찾고 있는 책
scenes.narration: 앨리스는 그림이 궁금해 나비의 책을 묻지 않고 가져왔어요. 앨리스는 책의 위치를 알지만 나비는 몰라요.
scenes.action: 앨리스는 책을 들고 있어요. 나비가 주변을 둘러봐요. 각 화자의 앞모습을 보여 줘요. 할머니의 예문은 연습 설명이지 사건 고백이 아니에요.

lines.speaker: 나비
lines.text: 책을 다시 보고 싶은데 찾을 수가 없어.

lines.speaker: 부엉이 할머니
lines.text: 내가 한 일을 말할 땐 “내가 그랬어”로 시작하고, 이유와 고칠 일을 덧붙일 수 있어.

scenes.title: 사실을 말하는 표현
scenes.narration: 앨리스가 나비에게 말할 때 쓸 표현을 우리에게 알려 줘요.
scenes.action: 앨리스는 아이를 향해 표현을 설명해요. 나비에게 실제로 고백하거나 책을 건네는 동작은 아직 없어요.

lines.speaker: 앨리스
lines.text: “내가 그랬어”는 영어로 “It was me”야. 내가 한 일을 인정하는 말이야. 이유를 설명해도 다른 사람 탓으로 돌리지는 않아.

scenes.title: 말을 꺼낼까?
scenes.narration: 나비는 아직 책이 어디 있는지 몰라요.
scenes.action: 선택한 갈래에서만 실제 고백해요. 두 갈래가 끝날 때까지 책은 앨리스가 계속 들고 있어요.

choices.label: 나비가 모르는 일을 알려 줘요
choices.action: 앨리스가 나비에게 걸어가 멈춘 뒤 앞모습으로 대사해요. 책을 아직 돌려주지 않아요.

lines.speaker: 앨리스
lines.text: 내가 그랬어. 그림을 보고 싶어서 묻지 않고 책을 가져갔어. 네가 찾을 줄은 생각하지 못했어. 미안해.

lines.speaker: 나비
lines.text: 나는 없어졌다고 생각했어. 지금 돌려주면 좋겠어.

lines.speaker: 앨리스
lines.text: 그래. 돌려주고 다음엔 먼저 물어볼게.

choices.label: 걱정되어 말을 미뤄요
choices.action: 앨리스는 책을 들고 말없이 잠깐 기다려요. 나비의 표정을 앞에서 보여 줘요. 할머니가 곁에 서고, 앨리스가 얼굴을 보여 주며 고백해요. 책은 아직 앨리스에게 있어요.

lines.speaker: 나비
lines.text: 어디 있는지 몰라서 답답하고 속상해.

lines.speaker: 앨리스
lines.text: 속상하게 할까 봐 말을 미뤘는데, 모르는 채 찾는 것도 힘들겠구나. 할머니, 같이 있어 주세요.

lines.speaker: 부엉이 할머니
lines.text: 곁에 있을게. 있었던 일을 말해 보렴.

lines.speaker: 앨리스
lines.text: 내가 그랬어. 물어보지 않고 책을 가져갔어. 내 선택이었어. 미안해. 돌려줄게.

lines.speaker: 나비
lines.text: 알려 줘서 고마워. 다음엔 찾기 전에 먼저 말해 줘.

scenes.title: 책을 돌려줄 때
scenes.narration: 이제 나비가 책을 받을 준비를 해요.
scenes.action: 둘이 서서 손이 닿는 거리를 확보해요. 앨리스의 “여기 있어”에 맞춰 나비에게 책을 한 번만 건네요. 나비의 답은 받은 뒤 해요. 두 친구가 앉아 말할 때도 얼굴을 보여 줘요. 마지막 초대에서는 앨리스가 정면으로 아이에게 말해요.

lines.speaker: 앨리스
lines.text: 여기 있어. 보고 싶어도 네 대답을 먼저 들을게.

lines.speaker: 나비
lines.text: 아직 조금 속상하지만 책이 돌아와서 마음은 편해졌어.

lines.speaker: 앨리스
lines.text: 네 마음을 말해 줘서 고마워. 지금은 네가 편하게 보도록 기다릴게.

lines.speaker: 앨리스
lines.text: 같이 “내가 그랬어”라고 해 볼까? 오늘 이야기 속 말만 연습해도 되고, 조용히 들어도 돼.

recall.prompt: 보리의 물뿌리개를 쓰고 다른 자리에 두었어. 보리가 찾을 때 누구 탓도 하지 않고 무엇과 위치를 말할 수 있을까? 듣기만 해도 돼.
recall.example: 내가 그랬어. 쓰고 나서 꽃밭에 두었어. 알려 주지 않아 미안해. 같이 찾아줄게.

versions.title: What I know, what Nabi knows
versions.goal: Consider the difficulty of telling and the friend’s missing information, then explain and repair
versions.setting: One book belonging to Nabi · path near the bench
versions.caregiverNote: A friend may still have feelings after the truth is told. Do not ask the child to disclose a real mistake.

scenes.title: The missing book
scenes.narration: Alice took Nabi’s book without asking because she wanted to see the pictures. Alice knows where it is; Nabi does not.
scenes.action: Alice holds the book. Nabi looks around. Keep each speaking face visible. Grandma’s example is a language model, not a confession about this event.

lines.speaker: Nabi
lines.text: I want to look at my book again, but I cannot find it.

lines.speaker: Grandma Owl
lines.text: You can begin with “It was me,” then explain what happened and what you will put right.

scenes.title: Words for telling what happened
scenes.narration: Alice shares words she can use before speaking to Nabi.
scenes.action: Alice explains the expression to the viewer. There is no actual confession to Nabi or book handoff yet.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “내가 그랬어” means “It was me” in English. It says I did the thing. I can explain why without blaming someone else.

scenes.title: Will Alice speak?
scenes.narration: Nabi still does not know where the book is.
scenes.action: The actual confession happens only inside the chosen path. Alice keeps holding the book through the end of either path.

choices.label: Tell Nabi what he does not know
choices.narration: Alice stops in front of Nabi.
choices.action: Alice walks to Nabi, stops, and speaks with her face visible. Do not return the book yet.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: It was me. I took the book without asking to see the pictures. I did not think about you searching. I’m sorry.

lines.speaker: Nabi
lines.text: I thought it was lost. I would like it back now.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: Okay. I’ll return it and ask first next time.

choices.label: Put off telling because of worry
choices.action: Alice holds the book during a short silent pause. Show Nabi’s face. Grandma stands nearby, then Alice confesses with her face visible. The book remains with Alice.

lines.speaker: Nabi
lines.text: Not knowing where it is makes me frustrated and upset.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: I worried that telling would upset him, but searching without knowing is hard too. Grandma, please stay with me.

lines.speaker: Grandma Owl
lines.text: I’m here. You can tell what happened.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: It was me. I took the book without asking. That was my choice. I’m sorry. I’ll give it back.

lines.speaker: Nabi
lines.text: Thank you for telling me. Next time, tell me before I have to search.

scenes.title: Time to return it
scenes.narration: Nabi is ready to receive the book.
scenes.action: Both stand within reach. Give the book once on Alice’s “Here it is.” Nabi answers after receiving it. If the friends sit, keep their speaking faces visible. For the final invitation, show Alice facing the child.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: Here it is. Even when I want a look, I’ll wait for your answer first.

lines.speaker: Nabi
lines.text: I’m still a little upset, but having my book back helps me feel calmer.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: Thank you for telling me how you feel. I’ll wait so you can look at it comfortably now.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: Shall we try “It was me”? We can practice just the story words. Quiet listening is welcome.

recall.prompt: You used Bori’s watering can and left it somewhere else. How could you explain what happened and where it is without blaming anyone? You may just listen.
recall.example: It was me. I left it in the garden after using it. I’m sorry I didn’t say. I’ll help you find it.
